items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I've seen the Monty Gras on TV and I'm telling you my heart almost cried. I'm telling you tears came to my eyes.

ctx.x: Bye-bye. This is January 3rd, 1961 and the subject of our interview is Mr. Charles Levy from New Orleans and you heard him read from his composition in the good old days in New Orleans. He didn't know that he was reading at the microphone but he was reading it to show me the spirit of some of the things he's written. voice besides mine and Mr. Levy's will be that of Ike Robinson who accompanied Mr. Levy today. The purpose of our tape or the purpose of the recording Mr. Levy is to provide the Tulane University…

born about a block from Esplanade Avenue, I think it was, on Barrick Street. Have you been back there lately? I haven't been there since 1914, but I said I want to go back. Oh, is that so? That's in my mind. I've seen the Monty Gras on TV and I'm telling you my heart almost cried. I'm telling you tears came to my eyes. I want to go back. Did you play when you were in LA? I was playing violin in a little group down there and just learning to put a little jazz in the violin, unbeknownst to my music teacher. Putting a
